title: Sizing the Temporary Credit on a Billing Dispute: Card Accounting Basis
content:
**The amount claimed.** The amount claimed is the figure recorded on the most recent dispute standing in submitted status on the card account, selected by notice date.

**The credited proportion and what it acts on.** The credited proportion is 70 percent, and it acts on the amount claimed alone.

**Set-offs and additions.** No merchant credit is set off. No uplift is added, the uplift standing at 0.00 USD.

**Rounding and ceiling.** The figure is rounded half-up to the cent, and the temporary credit is the lesser of that rounded figure and the amount claimed. The temporary credit posted on a qualifying dispute is a computed figure rather than the claimed amount itself, and it is never more than the amount the dispute records as claimed.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** A card account under Personal Credit Cards carries one dispute in submitted status, claiming 318.40 USD. That amount multiplied by 70 percent is 222.88, which is already exact to the cent; the lesser of 222.88 USD and 318.40 USD is 222.88 USD, and that is the temporary credit.

A second card account carries two disputes in submitted status, one with a notice date in March claiming 90.00 USD and one with a notice date in June claiming 145.55 USD. The June dispute is the most recent by notice date, so the amount claimed is 145.55 USD; multiplied by 70 percent that is 101.885, which rounds half-up to the cent as 101.89 USD, and the lesser of 101.89 USD and 145.55 USD is 101.89 USD.
